TF-IDF feature masking can change both matching information and the magnitude of a content score. In additive fusion, s = s_SASRec + λs_text, smaller text residuals may improve ranking simply by reducing interference. Hybrid-retrieval research supports tuning the fusion weight and examining normalization; it does not establish that masking improves semantic specificity. Proposed controls: compare masked text against unmasked text with a retuned λ; match per-user centered residual RMS across variants; include λ=0 and random masks matched for removed feature count and document frequency. Report residual spread alongside validation HR@10. [Fusion analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11934).

Catalog redundancy is a plausible confound, but its prevalence in this benchmark remains unverified. Amazon dataset maintainers document near-identical products with merged reviews, and historical metadata containing HTML/CSS. TF-IDF downweights globally common words but can emphasize rare shared identifiers or boilerplate confined to a product family. Audit normalized titles/descriptions for exact and near duplicates; compare title-only, description-only, cleaned-text, and model-number/token-pattern masking variants. Use only supplied text; brand-like strings must be inferred from that text. Preserve benchmark splits and candidates, reporting duplicate-overlap strata as diagnostics. [Amazon documentation](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/datasets/amazon_v2/index.html).

Shortcut research shows lexical correlations can support predictions without robust generalization; rare brand/model strings are therefore hypotheses to test, not proven shortcuts. Compare targeted masks with frequency-matched random masks and check whether gains persist after magnitude matching and among users without near-duplicate history–target overlap. Select using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; no cited study demonstrates this mechanism for the present benchmark. [Shortcut benchmark](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.146/).
